header: Date: 2027-11-29 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~72 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Liam (Redwood SE), Sanjay (NovaHarbor), Bethany (NovaHarbor), Marcus (NovaHarbor), Ivy (NovaHarbor)
summary: Kickoff to align on onboarding sprint, security requirements, baseline perf tests, and go-live runway. Agreed milestones: runbook + sprint plan, perf baseline, SSO details, weekly sync. Several technical constraints discussed: VPC peering, KMS, data retention and dedicated capacity sizing.
topics: onboarding plan, dedicated vs hosted, VPC/private control plane, SSO/SCIM, KMS and key handling, perf baseline and sample payloads, SLA expectations, rollouts and fallback plans
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'll kick things off. We wanted this to be the onboarding readiness workshop, run through the plan, and make sure we have all blockers surfaced. Apologies for any audio noise today.

[00:22] Sanjay Rao: Thanks Jordan. Quick ask — we run an internal cadence with platform and security, so would like to verify timelines. We're targeting pilot in mid-Jan, full go-live late Feb if all goes well.

[00:34] Maya Patel: Great, that timeline is reasonable. It gives us enough time for a two-sprint onboarding: 2 weeks integration + 4 weeks ramp and testing. We can adjust if you want more buffer.

[00:48] Bethany Cole: Two questions up front — one on network: do we need VPC peering or is a customer-managed private deployment required? Two, for cost — what's the difference in unit economics between your hosted API and Redwood Dedicated?

[01:05] Liam Ortiz: Good questions. For most customers we do VPC peering for the private control plane if you're on cloud; on-prem is also an option but longer lead time. Hosted API is fastest, but Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput. Cost-wise, Dedicated reduces per-token variance for steady qps. I can show a sample calc later.

[01:30] Marcus Lee: On security: we need to know about KMS integration and key ownership. We cannot have Redwood-owned keys for this pilot. Also logs — how long are audit logs kept and can we ship them to our SIEM?

[01:45] Jordan Park: Understood. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and Redwood can integrate to your KMS via standard APIs. Logs: we have configurable retention; for Dedicated/Private we can push audit logs to your syslog/S3 or CloudWatch. We'll attach the security docs.

[02:03] Ivy Chen: Also, product ops wants to understand rollback/rollout behavior — e.g., can we canary a model or pin versions?

[02:12] Liam Ortiz: Absolutely — the platform supports version pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a model fails. We'll walk through the Console controls in the demo.

[02:27] Sanjay Rao: For benchmarking: we have two workloads — low-latency chat (avg 250-400 tokens) and large document embeddings (avg 2k tokens). We need to see both scenarios so we can decide quantization + batching settings.

[02:45] Maya Patel: Perfect — that's helpful. Action item: Sanjay to send sample payloads and qps patterns. Liam, we'll set up the perf tests.

[03:00] Bethany Cole: Slight aside — we use Okta for SSO and SCIM. We'll need RBAC mapping to Okta groups, ideally syncing groups to roles in Redwood.

[03:12] Marcus Lee: And we need an audit trail for any model changes and who triggered rollouts. Retention should be at least 1 year for compliance.

[03:25] Jordan Park: We can support group-based RBAC, SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Audit trails are supported for Dedicated/Private deployments with retention settings. I'll mark that to confirm retention windows in the security doc.

[03:40] Liam Ortiz: Quick note on latency / cost tradeoff since you mentioned embeddings — for 2k tokens embedding jobs you might want batching and a higher memory variant or quantized model depending on accuracy needs. We'll recommend model/quantization profiles after we see sample data.

[04:02] Ivy Chen: How do you handle KV cache? For chat, we want prefix caching to save tokens and keep tail latencies low.

[04:11] Liam Ortiz: We have prefix + KV cache support; it reduces per-token costs for repeated contexts. There are configuration knobs: cache TTL, key-length thresholds, and shared vs per-session caches. We'll propose defaults based on test runs.

[04:32] Sanjay Rao: Any constraints around private deployments and air-gapped environments? We do have one customer team that's highly regulated.

[04:40] Jordan Park: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped needs but it requires additional lead time and an enterprise license. For your pilot, I suggest VPC private deployment with customer-managed control plane which handles most regulated needs.

[04:56] Bethany Cole: About telemetry — we'd like token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. Are those available in Redwood Console?

[05:04] Maya Patel: Yes — Console has route/model dashboards, token-breakdown and trace hooks. We'll enable a 90-day retention for the pilot and show how to export to your analytics stack.

[05:18] Marcus Lee: Are there any certs (SOC2/ISO) we should call out before pilots with real customer data?

[05:26] Jordan Park: Redwood currently has SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We'll share the cert pack and the relevant sections of our security questionnaire.

[05:36] Ivy Chen: Can you walk through a sample sprint plan? We want who does what week-by-week.

[05:45] Maya Patel: Sure — high level: Week 0: kickoff + access; Week 1: connectivity + SSO + basic API integration; Week 2: perf baseline + model selection; Weeks 3–4: pilot testing and validation; Week 5–6: ramp and go/no-go review. We'll provide a detailed runbook.

[06:12] Sanjay Rao: On connectivity: we need a checklist — firewall rules, ports, peering configs. Can you provide a cut-and-paste ready doc for our infra team?

[06:21] Liam Ortiz: Yes — I have a network checklist PDF and a table of ports/URLs. I'll add it to the runbook and share as a link.

[06:34] Bethany Cole: For the pilot, can we reserve Dedicated capacity or will it be mixed with hosted? We need predictable throughput for our customer-facing flow.

[06:45] Jordan Park: For pilot we can reserve a small Dedicated pool or we can do a private VPC with reserved nodes. Dedicated is ideal if you want strict SLOs; otherwise we can configure burst caps on hosted. We'll include a cost comparison in the runbook.

[07:00] Marcus Lee: Data residency — some PII stays in US-east only. Can we pin region for inference?

[07:08] Liam Ortiz: Yes, requests can be routed to region-specific pools. For Dedicated and Private you can pin region and also have routing policies.

[07:20] Ivy Chen: A practical question — what's the smallest unit of measurement for billing? Tokens per request or per-embedding? We need this for our cost model.

[07:29] Jordan Park: Hosted is billed per token and per embedding unit; Dedicated is a committed monthly capacity plus a small per-token delta for overage. We'll send the pricing sheet.

[07:40] Sanjay Rao: Ok, great. On the performance test — can you run both chat and embeddings in the same baseline so we can see mixed workload impact? We often run mixed queries.

[07:51] Liam Ortiz: Absolutely. We'll design a mixed workload test mirroring your qps curves and tail latencies. Also we'll note quantization differences and show quality deltas.

[08:05] Bethany Cole: Who's the day-to-day contact if we hit infra blockers?

[08:11] Maya Patel: That'll be me for ops and Jordan for commercial. Liam will be your tech lead for SE questions. We'll add escalation paths in the runbook.

[08:23] Marcus Lee: For compliance, we might need a data processing agreement and a subprocessor list. We'll need those reviewed by legal before the pilot.

[08:31] Jordan Park: We'll attach DPA and subprocessors in the follow-up email. Expect those in the security packet.

[08:41] Ivy Chen: Can you share example alert thresholds and what observability looks like for anomalies?

[08:48] Liam Ortiz: We'll share a recommended set: token rate sudden increase, error rate >1% sustained, 95th pct latency breach, and quality drift triggers if you want evals tied to prompt sets.

[09:05] Sanjay Rao: Last thing — how do we handle model updates mid-pilot? We don't want surprises.

[09:12] Jordan Park: We'll lock model versions for the pilot and enable controlled rollouts in the Console. Any update requires signer approval from your side in the change control doc.

[09:25] Maya Patel: Quick recap and next steps: Jordan will send runbook and pricing; Liam will schedule perf runs and share network checklist; Sanjay will provide workloads and qps patterns; Marcus will confirm compliance scoping; Maya to send weekly meeting invite.

[09:42] Sanjay Rao: Sounds good. Let's set the first weekly sync for 2027-12-07.

[09:48] Jordan Park: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and documents.

[09:55] Bethany Cole: Thanks all.

[10:00] End of recording. Note: transcript contains occasional mis-attributed phrases and filler words; minor ASR errors may exist (e.g., K V cache transcribed as cash).
